The main pipeline programs: extraction, per-sample clustering and population clustering.

Generated from the `--help` output of SeekDeep 3.0.2-dev. Run `SeekDeep <command> --help` to see the same for your installed version. Commands and flags are not case sensitive, and every command also takes `--help`/`-h` and `--getFlags`.

## extractor {#extractor}

Extract sequences from various sequences input types (fastq,fasta,etc.) with primers and barcodes plus some filtering

```bash
SeekDeep extractor --help
```

**Required Options**

*ID File*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--id` | The name of the ID file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*Reading Sequence Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fasta` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fasta text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastagz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fasta gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastqgz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

## extractorByKmerMatching {#extractorByKmerMatching}

Extract each target's reads from one sample's long reads (e.g. nanopore or pacbio) by the target k-mers they share, from genTargetInfoFromGenomes, then check primers, length and quality, reads of several targets are split into one read per target. Writes passing and failing reads per target plus extractionProfile.tab.txt and extractionStats.tab.txt to the output directory

```bash
SeekDeep extractorByKmerMatching --help
```

**Required Options**

*IDs*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ids`<br>`--id` | Primers file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--lenCutOffsFnp`<br>`--lenCutOffs` | Length cut offs per target, e.g. forSeekDeep/lenCutOffs.txt from genTargetInfoFromGenomes **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--uniqueKmersPerTarget` | The per target k-mer table, e.g. forSeekDeep/uniqueKmers.tab.txt.gz or allKmers.tab.txt.gz from genTargetInfoFromGenomes **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*Reading Sequence Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bam` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, bam file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fasta` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fasta text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastagz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fasta gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastqgz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*IDs*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--refSeqDir` | reference Seq Dir, should have a .fasta file named by each target |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*K-mer Stretch Trim*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kmerStretchTrimSlop` | Bases kept past each primer when trimming to a target's k-mer stretch, for reads whose first or last unique k-mer is further in because of sequencing errors. The primer ends up about this far into the trimmed read, reads that have been cut are always searched at least this far in | `40` | uint32_t |
| `--noKmerStretchTrim` | Don't trim reads of one target to that target's stretch of the read. By default a read assigned to a single target is cut back to the stretch covered by k-mers unique to that target (the same stretches the multihit split finds) plus the target's primer and --kmerStretchTrimSlop on each side, so sequence that belongs to no target, e.g. a human off-target product ligated onto the amplicon, no longer keeps the primers outside the primer search window. Only reads that wouldn't pass as they are (primers, length and quality) get trimmed, so a read that passes without trimming is never changed. On 200k reads, ligation Pool 2 passed 32.5% more reads with it (as many as --primerWithinStart 2000), mostly amplicons with human sequence ligated on, and run 3 (PCR barcoding) 0.5% more | `false` | bool |

*MID*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--MIDAllowableErrors` | Number of errors to allow in MIDs, more errors allowed can lead to mis-sorting of reads by MIDs | `1` | uint32_t |

*Multihit Split*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--multihitSplitMaxGap` | Largest gap between a target's unique k-mer hits within one stretch of a multihit read | `100` | uint32_t |
| `--multihitSplitMinKmers` | Unique k-mer hits a stretch of a multihit read needs to count as a target's amplicon | `20` | uint32_t |
| `--multihitSplitOneEnd` | Multihit reads demultiplexed on one end's barcode (barcodeEnds=1 in the name): none leaves them as multihit, nearest keeps only the amplicon nearest that barcode (needs assignedOn and direction in the name), all keeps every piece. Pieces of one end reads are tagged barcodeEnds=1, so they only add to a sample-target that also has both ends reads (processClusters --minBothEndsBarcodeReads); some of these pieces come from other samples' molecules, and without that filter they put 268-444 reads on 5 targets in ligation Pool 1's no template controls. With the filter, all kept the controls clean and raised final reads by 38% (run 2), 67% (Pool 1) and 13% (Pool 2). Reads without barcodeEnds are always split | `all` | std::string |
| `--multihitSplitPrimerSlop` | Sequence kept on each side of a stretch past the longest primer, so the primers are still found | `20` | uint32_t |
| `--noMultihitSplit` | Don't split reads that hit several targets; by default each target's stretch of the read (found by k-mers unique to that target) is extracted as its own read, e.g. amplicons ligated end to end | `false` | bool |

*Output Directory*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dout` | Output Directory Name | `./` | std::string |
| `--overWriteDir` | If the directory already exists over write it | `false` | bool |

*Post Processing*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--qualCheckCutOff` | The fractions of bases that have to be above the qualCheckLevel to be kept | `0.15` | double |
| `--qualCheckLevel` | Bin qualities at this quality to do filtering on fraction above this | `30` | unsigned char |

*Primer*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--primerCoverage` | Amount of primers found | `0.5` | double |
| `--primerMoreThan2BaseIndels` | Number Of greater than two base indels to allow in primers | `0.99` | double |
| `--primerNumOfMismatches` | Number of Mismatches to allow in primers | `5` | uint32_t |
| `--primerOneBaseIndels` | Number Of One base indels to allow in primers | `4` | double |
| `--primerTwoBaseIndels` | Number Of Two base indels to allow in primers | `2` | double |
| `--primerUpper` | Leave primers in upper case | `false` | bool |

*Primers*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--primerSearchStart` | By default the primers are searched at the very beginning of seq, use this flag to start the search here | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--primerWithinStart` | How far into the read the primers are searched for. Reads that were cut to their target (split reads of several targets, --noKmerStretchTrim, --trimPrimers) are searched at least 50 bases in, or as far in as the cut left the primers, so this doesn't need to be raised for sequence in front of the primers; kept low it keeps down false positives, and joined amplicons from passing whole | `50` | uint32_t |

*Reading Sequence Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--lower` | How to handle Lower Case Bases | `nothing` | std::string |
| `--processed` | Processed, Input Sequence Name has a suffix that contains abundance info | `false` | bool |
| `--removeGaps` | Remove Gaps from Input Sequences | `false` | bool |
| `--trimAtWhiteSpace` | Remove everything after first whitespace character in input sequence name | `false` | bool |

*Trim Primers*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--trimKmersPerTarget` | The k-mers per trimming region, from genTargetInfoFromGenomes run on --trimPrimers |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--trimLenCutOffs` | The length cut offs per trimming region, from genTargetInfoFromGenomes run on --trimPrimers |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--trimPrimers` | Primers, in the same format as --id, that mark off regions within the amplified targets to trim the reads to. With these, --id, --lenCutOffs and --uniqueKmersPerTarget describe the amplified targets and are only used to work out which target a read is, split reads of several targets and drop foldbacks; a read doesn't need the amplified primers or the amplified target's length. Each read is cut to every region of its target it covers, and only the trimming primers, the region's length and the quality are checked. A target can have several regions, they can overlap, and each region is output as its own target. Regions are matched to the amplified targets by their k-mers |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--trimRegionMinKmers` | The k-mer hits needed to find a trimming region in a read | `10` | uint32_t |
| `--trimRegionSlop` | Bases kept past each trimming primer for finding it, for reads whose first or last k-mer is further in because of sequencing errors | `40` | uint32_t |

|---|---|---|---|

| `--out` | Out Filename | `out` | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--outExtention` | Extension of out file |  | std::string |
| `--outFormat` | Format of out sequence file |  | std::string |
| `--overWrite` | Over Write Existing Files | `false` | bool |

*filtering*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--hardKmersPerTarget` | hard occurencet cut off Kmers Per Target | `5` | uint32_t |
| `--kmerFracPerTarget` | at minimum have to have this fraction of kmers in a Target | `0.1` | double |
| `--maxLenCutOff` | Hard cut off max length | `10000` | uint32_t |
| `--minLenCutOff` | Hard cut off min length | `100` | uint32_t |

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ignoreMissingKmerSets` | ignore Missing Kmer Sets | `false` | bool |
| `--noInvertedKmerIndex` | Probe every target's k-mer set for every read k-mer instead of using one k-mer -\> target(s) index. The index gives identical counts, counting a k-mer shared between targets toward each of them exactly as the probe does; this exists to fall back if that is ever in doubt | `false` | bool |
| `--numThreads` | number of threads | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--rename` | rename input extracted reads | `false` | bool |
| `--sampleName` | sample name, if input is a bam this defaults to the SM of the read group in the header otherwise the input file's basename |  | std::string |

## extractorPairedEnd {#extractorPairedEnd}

Extract sequences from various sequences input types (fastq,fasta,sff,etc.) with primers and barcodes plus some filtering

```bash
SeekDeep extractorPairedEnd --help
```

**Required Options**

*ID File*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--id` | The name of the ID file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

*Post Processing*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--overlapStatusFnp` | A file with two columns, target,status, e.g. overlapStatuses.txt from genTargetInfoFromGenomes; status is one or more, comma separated, of R1BeginsInR2, R1EndsInR2, PerfectOverlap, NoOverlap or Auto (capitalization doesn't matter). R1BeginsInR2=target size \< read length (causes read through), R1EndsInR2=target size \> read length but less than 2 x read length, NoOverlap=target size \> 2 x read length and can't be combined with the others **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

| `--minPrimerMatchBases` | For the primer dimer report, the fewest bases of a primer that have to match at a read's end for it to be trusted, 0 to work it out from the number of primers since the more primers there are the more likely a short match is by chance | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--noPrimerDimerReport` | Don't write primerDimerCounts.tab.txt, which stitches all the pairs and looks for primers at both ends of the ones short enough to read through each other, it doesn't change which reads get kept | `false` | bool |

*Primers*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--primerSearchStart` | By default the primers are searched at the very beginning of seq, use this flag to start the search here | `0` | uint32_t |
| `--primerWithinStart` | By default the primers are searched at the very beginning of seq, use this flag to extended the search, should be kept low to cut down on false positives | `0` | uint32_t |

*Reading Sequence Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--lower` | How to handle Lower Case Bases | `nothing` | std::string |
| `--processed` | Processed, Input Sequence Name has a suffix that contains abundance info | `false` | bool |
| `--removeGaps` | Remove Gaps from Input Sequences | `false` | bool |
| `--trimAtWhiteSpace` | Remove everything after first whitespace character in input sequence name | `false` | bool |

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--debug` | Debug | `false` | bool |
| `--defaultOverlapStatus` | Set a overlap status for all targets, can be 1 of 5 values(case insensitive), AUTO, R1BEGINSINR2, R1ENDSINR2, NOOVERLAP, ALL. ALL=(R1BEGINSINR2 and R1ENDSINR2). Setting to auto will go with the status was most commonly found for a target, this can be dangerous as with unspecific amplification this can end up being set as the incorrect status | `auto` | std::string |
| `--keepFilteredOff` | Keep Filtered Off | `false` | bool |
| `--keepUnfilteredReads` | Keep the unfiltered reads for debugging purposes | `false` | bool |
| `--noTrimLowQualWindows` | Don't Trim Low Qual Windows | `false` | bool |
| `--numThreads` | Number of threads to use for finding the primers, the output is the same no matter the number of threads | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--primerCallCacheMaxEntries` | Max number of distinct read starts to remember the primer determination for so identical read starts don't have to be searched again, the output is the same with or without it, memory used is about this number times (primer window size + 100) bytes, set to 0 to turn off | `200000` | uint32_t |
| `--primerDimerSize` | Size of r1 begins in r2 stitched reads that should be considered primer dimers | `100` | uint32_t |
| `--qWindowSize` | Quality Window Trim Size | `5` | uint32_t |
| `--qWindowStep` | Quality Window Trim Step | `1` | uint32_t |
| `--qWindowTrimAvgQualCutOff` | Quality Window Trim Avg Qual Cut Off | `25` | double |
| `--stitchCacheMaxEntries` | Max number of mate pairs to remember the alignment of so that they only have to be aligned once when stitching, 0 to not remember any, the output is the same either way | `500000` | uint32_t |
| `--verbose`<br>`-v` | Verbose | `false` | bool |

*The id file should be tab delimited and contains the primer and reverse primer and MIDs if the data is multiplex, example below*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | target	forwardPrimer	reversePrimer |  |  |
|  | PFMSP1	AACTAGAAGCTTTAGAAGATGCA	ACATATGATTGGTTAAATCAAAG |  |  |
|  | PFMSP2	AGATGCAGCTTTAACTAGAAGAA	TTAAAACATATGATTGGTCAAAG |  |  |
|  | id	barcode |  |  |
|  | MID01		ACGAGTGCGT |  |  |
|  | MID02		ACGCTCGACA |  |  |

## kluster {#kluster}

Cluster one sample's reads of one target by k-mer similarity, the alternative to qluster for high error rate reads like nanopore and pacbio. Writes the clusters to output (in the input's format) and outputInfo.tab.txt in the output directory, ready for processClusters

Also callable as `kmerClusteringRate`.

```bash
SeekDeep kluster --help
```

**Required Options**

*Reading Sequence Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bam` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, bam file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fasta` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fasta text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastagz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fasta gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq1` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq first mate text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq1gz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq first mate gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq2` | Input sequence filename, only needed with --fastq1, fastq second mate text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq2gz` | Input sequence filename, only needed with --fastq1gz, fastq second mate gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastqgz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--sff` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, sff text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--sffBin` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, sff binary file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

## makeSampleDirectories {#makeSampleDirectories}

Make the directory tree processClusters reads from a table of sample names, one directory per sample with a subdirectory per replicate, plus locationByIndex/ with a file per index listing where each of its replicates went

```bash
SeekDeep makeSampleDirectories --help
```

**Required Options**

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dout` | Main Out Directory Name **(required)** |  | std::string |
| `--file` | Tab (or whitespace) delimited sample names file, at least 3 columns: 1) index (or input file) name, 2) sample name, 3+) the replicate (e.g. MID) names for that sample, e.g. a row of 1 090-00 MID01 MID02 is sample 090-00 with replicates MID01 and MID02 from index 1, rows starting with # are skipped **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*Miscellaneous*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--overWriteDir` | If the directory already exists over write it | `false` | bool |
| `--separatedDirs` | Create a separate directory for each index, with the sample directories under it | `false` | bool |
| `--verbose`<br>`-v` | Verbose | `false` | bool |

## qluster {#qluster}

Cluster input sequences by collapsing on set differences between the sequences

Also callable as `clusterDown`.

```bash
SeekDeep qluster --help
```

**Required Options**

*Clustering*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--par` | Parameters filename to supply differences to allow to cluster, required unless technology flag used **(required)** |  | std::string |

*Reading Sequence Input*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fasta` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fasta text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastagz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fasta gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastq` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq text file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |
| `--fastqgz` | Input sequence filename, only need 1, fastq gzipped file **(required)** |  | boost::filesystem::path |

**Optional Options**

*Additional Output*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--additionalOut` | Additional out filename for sorting final results |  | std::string |
| `--createMinTree` | Create Pseudo minimum Spanning Trees For Mismatches for Final Clusters | `false` | bool |
| `--snapShots` | Output Snap Shots of clustering results after each iteration | `false` | bool |
| `--writeOutFinalAllByAllComparison` | Write out all pairwise comparisons between all the final clusters | `false` | bool |
| `--writeOutFinalInternalSnps` | Write out Internal (within the clusters) SNP class, useful for debugging if over collapsing is happening | `false` | bool |
| `--writeOutInitalSeqs` | Write out the sequences that make up each cluster | `false` | bool |

*Alignment*

| Flag | Description | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--caseInsensitive` | Use Case Insensitive Scoring for alignment | `false` | bool |
| `--countEndGaps` | Count End Gaps | `false` | bool |
| `--degen` | Use Degenerative Base Scoring for alignment | `false` | bool |
| `--gap` | Gap Penalties for Middle Gap | `5,1` | std::string |
| `--gapAll` | Gap Penalties for All (middle and end gaps) | `5,1` | std::string |
| `--gapLeft` | Gap Penalties for Left End Gap | `5,1` | std::string |
| `--gapRight` | Gap Penalties for Right End Gap | `0,0` | std::string |
| `--lessN` | Use Degenerative Base Scoring but use a lesser score for the degenerative bases | `false` | bool |
| `--local` | Local alignment | `false` | bool |
| `--match` | Match score for alignment | `2` | int32_t |
| `--mismatch` | Mismatch score for alignment | `-2` | int32_t |
| `--noAlignCompare` | Do comparisons without globally aligning | `false` | bool |
| `--noHomopolymerIndelWeighting` | Don't do Homopolymer Weighting | `false` | bool |
| `--scoreMatrix` | Score Matrix Filename |  | std::string |
| `--use_blosum62` | Use blosum62 scoring | `false` | bool |

| `--chiPosSpacing` | The amount of shared sequence inbetween difference to consider a sequence a chimera of two parent sequences | `3` | uint32_t |
| `--noMarkChimeras` | Don't do chimera marking | `false` | bool |
